incident-bot: :rotating_light: HIGH - GPU queue growth observed in eu-west-1 · 12:03 UTC - 3 service routes showing sustained enqueue >30s. Auto-scaler failing to reach desired capacity. Paging oncall: @Maya (oncall)
Maya (oncall): on it, pulling logs now. seeing api/generate queues jump from ~100 -> 2.5k in the last 8m. throttles firing. any immediate mitigation ideas?
Sanjay (infra): checking autoscaler events. Looks like scaleup loop is hitting cloud provider quota and then we have scheduler rejecting pods due to insufficient MIG-sized slots. Fwiw there are many small MIG slices leftover from recent canary.
Ben (runtime): sounds like fragmentation — we have capacity in total GPUs but not in contiguous MIG sizes to satisfy instanceSelectors. Pods are Pending with reason: "Insufficient GPU".
Zara (sre): customers reporting 429s and increased latency. Lena, any CS first reports?
Lena (Customer Success): 3 customers opened tickets, mentioning timeouts on embeddings and model generation. Priority clients A and B affected intermittently. We told them we're investigating and will update in 15m.
Maya (oncall): escalation path: 1) throttle lower-priority jobs 2) add temporary fallback routes (cpu-ephemeral or smaller models) 3) emergency scale (if possible) 4) manual binpack/evacuate. Starting step 1 now.
ops-bot: Throttle policy applied: set route-priority for 'research' -> low. Affected routes reduced token throughput by 60%.
Ben (runtime): applying temporary reroute: api/generate -> model-reduced-1 (smaller architecture) for non-critical tenants, patching router.
Sanjay (infra): autoscaler logs paste:
```
I0312 12:07:14 autoscaler] desired=24 current=18 provisioning=0 error=quota_exceeded: Insufficient capacity (GPUs).
I0312 12:07:14 scheduler] pod/predict-xyz Pending: 4 nodes fit, 0 nodes available due to MIG size mismatch (need 7g.20, only 3g.5 fragments).
```
Maya (oncall): ok quota_exceeded explains cloud API failing. We should free up existing stranded GPUs. Any safe candidates to kill preemptively?
Ben (runtime): listing running jobs - found a set of long-running low-priority batch evals on node-a100-17 consuming full MIG slices. Suggest evicting those.
Sanjay (infra): starting controlled eviction: cordon node-a100-17, drain with --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data; low-priority pods annotated 'preemptible=true'.
Zara (sre): watch customer impact — moving traffic could spike latencies temporarily. Notify CS.
Lena (Customer Success): alerted affected customers: "we're moving lower-priority workloads off GPUs to restore capacity; will update in 10m."
Maya (oncall): also toggled scheduler policy to relax instanceSelector matching for 10m to allow pod to land on slightly different MIG slice. This is an emergency change.
Ben (runtime): applied scheduler override patch (rolled back auto-rollback scheduled in 30m). Code snippet:
```
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
data:
  schedulerOverrides: |
    allowMismatchedMIG=true
```
Sanjay (infra): after evictions and override, nodes accepted several pending pods, queue drain rate improved. Queue now down to ~400.
Maya (oncall): good. starting to scale back throttles slowly. Ops-bot: metrics?
ops-bot: queue_size(api/generate) 12:22 -> 412 -> 78 over 18m. 5xx error spikes down to baseline.
Ben (runtime): still seeing ~2 stranded GPUs reported by node-exporter due to MIG misalignment — they show healthy but not schedulable because of orphaned minor slices. I can run the MIG reprofile script to consolidate but it requires draining whole physical GPUs which is riskier.
Sanjay (infra): cloud provider quotas still blocking new instances, but we don't need new nodes now. Main risk: repeated fragmentation from nightly canaries that create tiny MIGs. Need longer-term fix.
Zara (sre): summary for now: immediate incident mitigated by throttling + evicting low-priority jobs + scheduler relax override. Impact: ~12 tenants saw elevated timeouts, 2 enterprise customers had short outages (~3-10m).
Maya (oncall): handing off to Sanjay for infra remediation and Ben for runtime follow-up. I'll remain on the thread for customer updates.
Sanjay (infra): next steps I'm running MIG-consolidate plan during low-traffic window. Plan: 1) pick 6 nodes with fragmented MIGs 2) cordon & drain 3) reconfigure MIG profiles (merge slices) 4) uncordon. ETA 2h. Posting runbook link: https://internal/runbooks/mig-consolidate
Ben (runtime): I'll audit instanceSelector constraints across deployments and create a hotfix to prefer binpacking-aware placement instead of strict matching. Will open PR and cherry-pick to canary.
Lena (Customer Success): customers updated. They asked for root cause once we have it, and for a permanent SLA note for Dedicated customers.
Maya (oncall): incident classification: partial outage -> P2. Starting incident document and will assign postmortem. Handoff complete.
Sanjay (infra): running preflight checks for consolidation. Noting one complication: some nodes host stateful in-progress long-run sessions (KV caches). Will coordinate with Ben to avoid evicting active sessions.
Ben (runtime): ack, marking those pods no-evict. We'll migrate their traffic to warm-swap nodes first.
Zara (sre): logging the timeline for postmortem. Key learnings to capture: - autoscaler should surface quota rejection quicker and auto-relief path - avoid creating many tiny MIG slices in canaries - have a fast-path to consolidate MIGs without full drain - make scheduler more flexible for emergency fallbacks.
Maya (oncall): final live update to #incidents and status page at 12:45 UTC: service degraded -> recovering.
ops-bot: Incident note created: https://internal/incidents/1801204321. Assigned to infra-runbook.
Sanjay (infra): taking ownership. Will post progress updates.
Maya (oncall): handing off to Ben for next 30m to track runtime hotfixes, I'm moving to monitoring for CS updates.
Ben (runtime): starting PR now and will coordinate canary after consolidation.
Zara (sre): closing paging loop for now; escalation channel on if something regresses.
Maya (oncall): thanks all, good triage.
